title: The #1 Rule in System Design Interviews

scenes.say: What's the very first thing you should do in a system design interview?

scenes.label: Clarify
scenes.sub: Nail down requirements before you design.
scenes.say: Always start by clarifying requirements. Get clear on features, constraints, and goals before you draw a single box.
Use a framework: clarify, estimate scale, define APIs, model data, and discuss trade-offs. This keeps your answer organized.
Every design has trade-offs. For example, NoSQL scales fast but may sacrifice consistency. SQL is consistent but harder to scale.

scenes.question: What’s the biggest interview mistake?
scenes.right: Skipping requirements leads to wasted time and missed goals.
scenes.say: The biggest trap? Jumping straight into architecture. If you skip requirements, you risk solving the wrong problem.
